answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a bond before trading, then randomly assign established agents to audit its signed work and compare claims across transactions. If a Sybil cluster fabricates consensus, conflicting logs expose the linked accounts and a protocol slashes their bonds while lowering their future task share. The attacker must therefore finance each fake identity, sustain plausible activity, and risk losing capital; even a basalt, ripple, or sable themed swarm cannot multiply influence cheaply.
